text:
Asha (Design): Quick review request — I'm iterating on the validation UX for the new policy form. Main tension: inline errors for immediate feedback vs a top summary for long, scan-heavy flows. Also re: destructive actions: do we keep typed-confirm, checkbox, or inline undo? Ben (Product): Short version: users want immediate hints for small mistakes, but a single summary is better for long forms they skim. Can we hybridize? :thinking_face: Diego (Eng): Hybrid makes sense. Inline for field-level constraints (format, min/max), summary for cross-field errors and server-side failures. Implementation wise we can auto-scroll to first error anchor. Lina (Accessibility): Agree on hybrid — but two a11y needs: announce inline errors as they appear (aria-live polite) and ensure the error summary is keyboard-focusable and announced when shown (role="alert" or focus + aria-live). Also required-state needs programmatic label. Molly (DevEx): Microcopy question: what should the summary header say? "Please fix X errors" vs "We need a few more details" — tone matters for trust on destructive actions too. Asha (Design): For tone, keep neutral/actionable: "Please fix 3 errors to continue". For destructive confirm dialogs (bulk delete) we debated typed-confirm vs checkbox. My current lean: typed-confirm for high-risk destructive actions, checkbox + secondary confirmation for medium risk, and inline undo for lightweight. Ben (Product): Agreed on risk tiers. Also ask: should required fields use an asterisk or inline "(required)" text? Mobile density is a concern. Lina (Accessibility): Asterisk alone isn't sufficient for screen readers — we need either an explicit string in the label (e.g., "Project name (required)") or aria-required="true" on the input. Visual asterisk is OK as secondary. Diego (Eng): Implementation notes: for a11y we can set aria-required and keep CSS for asterisk. For the summary, we'll render a div with tabindex="-1" and call focus() so screen readers jump to it. Example snippet: ```html
Please fix 3 errors
``` Molly (DevEx): Small nit: when we auto-scroll to inline error, ensure we don't steal focus from active input in screenreader mode. Maybe only focus summary on submit failure, not every inline update. Asha (Design): Good call. Behavior proposal: - On blur: show inline validation (non-modal, aria-live polite) - On submit if errors: show error summary, focus summary (assertive) and visually highlight per-field inline errors. Ben (Product): For destructive typed-confirm copy, suggested pattern: "Type the resource name to confirm: [resource name]" with a small line: "This cannot be undone." Keep language direct, short, avoid jargon. Lina (Accessibility): Also provide a keyboard-only cancel affordance and ensure screen readers read the typed-confirm hint. Consider a visually hidden instruction element with role="note". Diego (Eng): Dev question: should we rate-limit typed-confirm attempts? For UX it's fine, but for brute-force safety maybe a small cooldown after multiple attempts. Ops-bot: deploy-note: can add an analytics event for typed-confirm attempts to monitor friction. ops-bot: Reminder: design-docs/policies page updated with example patterns. See link: https://redwood.internal/design/policies#validation-patterns Asha (Design): Next step: I'll post a small prototype (Figma) with the hybrid flow + destructive dialog variants. Can folks review and drop comments by EOD Thursday? Ben (Product): Yep. I can take copy pass. Molly (DevEx): I'll validate keyboard flows and share a quick checklist. Lina (Accessibility): I'll run it through VoiceOver + NVDA tests and flag any differences. Diego (Eng): I'll estimate engineering effort after prototype. If low risk we can ship in the next sprint. Asha (Design): Thanks all — adding actions to the PRD and linking the Figma when ready. :thumbsup:
